why_trail.why: Handoff and ruling align: equality predicate staying pure, git-toplevel resolution at the one impure call site, fail-closed on unresolvable cwd, one authorized test migration. Purity test reads co_names so a cwd=None branch cannot trip it; fixture repos must be real git repos to keep pass-path coverage real.

The regression is real and reproduced through main() with real git repos: containment lets <primary>/.worktrees/<slug> drive a primary-stamped spine. Red is captured, so the coming green is meaningful.

Equality plus call-site git-toplevel resolution closes the nested-worktree hole: git reports a linked worktree as its own toplevel, so a primary-stamped spine no longer matches from inside .worktrees/<slug>, while subdirectories of the right worktree resolve to its root and still pass. cwd=None fails closed only after the malformed-origin fallbacks, preserving no-raise fallback behavior.

Migration lands exactly as ruled: the synthetic subdirectory case flips to refusal with a docstring pointing at its new call-site home; the property itself is proven through main() against real git repos (fixtures now git-init worktree AND foreign as distinct siblings, so pass paths exercise real toplevel resolution, not the fail-closed branch); fail-closed pinned at predicate (cwd=None) and main() (non-git tempdir) levels; fallback stays senior to fail-closed so malformed origins never lock out or raise.

Full verification holds: green everywhere the baseline was green, plus 7 new tests and one un-skip that pre-dates the diff. The one count below baseline (skips 6 vs 7) is proven diff-independent by a stash experiment. The explorer-fixture repair is the ruling's fail-closed rule meeting the last non-git fixture standing; flagged as a scope misfit for review.

IMPLEMENTER_RESULT written to the handoff-named path with the verbatim red/green pair, mechanical count derivations, the flagged out-of-scope fixture repair, and the spine_rail lexical/git note routed as documentation deliverable.
